Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode` is trying to write a directory with a non-ASCII name into a TAR archive using `TarArchiveOutputStream`, with the option `setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames` set to true. The current bug report describes an issue where trying to add a directory with a name longer than 100 bytes generates an exception related to writing PAX headers.

Looking at the code of `setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames(boolean)`, it simply sets a boolean field `addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames` to the provided value without any additional logic or validation.

Based on this information, the issue seems to be related to the length of the directory name exceeding the limit of 100 bytes and causing an exception when writing PAX headers. The lack of handling or validation for long directory names in `TarArchiveOutputStream` might be the root cause of the problem.

Next, I will provide the best locations to be fixed.
```
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
